added_doc_lines: - **Canary and deploy hold.** The on-box owner arms `/var/lib/bts-deploy/hold`, stops the scheduler, drains writers, stages the tested SHA, checks readiness and verifies production activation. Failure keeps the hold, stops the guarded jobs and attempts containment and paging. Recovery is by verified fix forward.

- **Before the first guarded deploy**, run `bash scripts/install-systemd-hetzner.sh` as `bts` from the target revision and verify the user manager reloaded. The scheduler, dashboard and lineup collector unit templates now use `uv run --no-sync`. Preflight refuses stale loaded units at `guard`.

- **Install the guard as root** with `scripts/install-deploy-guard-hetzner.sh` from the target revision. Re-run it whenever the target's installer bytes change. A missing or mismatched fingerprint refuses at `guard-stale`. Verify the loaded scheduler condition and guarded cron through checklist A7.
- **The 01:00 grading cron can run until about 06:00 ET.** A busy writer refuses deployment before arm. Wait for the writer and verify a new sleep window.

- Every push to `deploy` selects its tested triggering SHA. The owner resets to that SHA as `bts`, syncs locked dependencies, restarts the dashboard and verifies scheduler activation. For an unavailable heartbeat Eric uses `recover_sha` through the recovery checks in INCIDENT §5.
- The on-box owner arms a durable hold before resetting to the triggering SHA. It stops
the scheduler, drains writers, syncs locked dependencies and checks candidate readiness
and the dashboard. In enter mode the canary requires usable contest state for the sampled
ET date. The owner starts production and durably clears the hold after verification.
Failure keeps the candidate checkout in place and closes the guarded jobs. Recovery is
by verified fix forward.
- ✅ **Ship it** by pushing to `deploy` after the checks in §5.
This is a full deploy of the selected `deploy` SHA, subject to §5.
- **Deploy failed or its result is unknown.** Read the Actions result, then use the run ID
to inspect the on-box result and `bts-deploy-hold status` read-only. Status exit 1
is expected for a hold. If the result or containment is uncertain, contact Eric before
any retry. Keep the hold and preserve pick, receipt, saver and streak files. Verify
today's ET slate, the original Bluesky delivery and MLB entry read-only. Use the dashboard
for inspection. A missing receipt, preview or alert authorizes no entry or resend. A
delivery may already have been admitted during activation.
- **Contest-state refusal.** Read `bts season-contract status`. On a dated day, verify MLB
has settled the prior slate before entering today's observation. Rerun only inside a
verified window. If delivery or entry is uncertain, or the window is too short, keep
the hold and report to Eric.
- **Partial sync.** Repair dependencies through a deploy of the intended revision. Check
stop and paging evidence. A 2xx response records HTTP acceptance. If checkout monitoring
is unavailable, consult the rehearsed missed-ping path.
- **Hand release (Eric only).** Confirm the intended revision, current ET state, prior
delivery and MLB entry and the recovery window before running
`bts-deploy-hold release --by-hand --reason "<reason>"`. The command checks the clean
checkout, loaded guard, installed cron, canary and offline locked uv check. Keep the hold
if any prerequisite is uncertain. Cron and boot can run as soon as the hold clears.
Recheck the window before using `systemctl --user start bts-scheduler` as `bts`.
- **Calibration warning after verified activation.** Record the warning and inspect
`data/.last_deploy_iso` read-only. The previous cutoff can remain in use.
- **After verified recovery.** Review grading, reconciliation and observation gaps read-only.
Backfill in verified chronological order after Eric checks the dates, the applied results
and the current streak.
## 5. Deploy and recovery
git push origin main:deploy          # ship inside the verified window
> `protect-main-deploy` ruleset will reject it.
Eric verifies the intended revision, season state, configured delivery, prior send and
MLB entry and a safe sleep window before shipping or retrying. A revert must serve the
current season with today's state and installed jobs. Commit `619abda7` cannot serve 2027.
For writer contention, wait for completion and verify a new window. For a refused window,
recheck the current slate and prior delivery and entry before retrying. A rerun through
`workflow_dispatch` performs a full deploy. When the heartbeat is absent, stale or unreadable,
Eric supplies `recover_sha`, the exact 40-hex target, after verifying prior delivery and entry
and a safe window. That input authorizes only the specified SHA.
- **Scheduler heartbeat.** A hold, a missing fresh heartbeat after release or missed pings
can take this check down. Box liveness remains independent. The 08:30 day-outcome DM
reports yesterday by its own evidence.

| A5 | **DM and cron configuration.** Restored-box execution follows R and B8a. Verify the root guard before installing guarded cron, and verify the current ET slate and window before starting the scheduler.
  • Restore `pick_delivery = "dm"` in `~/.bts-orchestrator.toml` (snapshot `.bak-20260914-season-over`). Once watchdog P4 (`1c0e759`) is deployed, also set `[scheduler] entry_intent = "enter"`: install refuses without an agreeing intent.
  • Run `bash scripts/cron-setup-hetzner.sh install` (`set -a && . ./.env && set +a` first). That re-enables `check-pick-entered` (with P4: only for `entry_intent = "enter"`) and installs the C-03 07:40 reconcile line.
  • Restart inside a sleep window.

| B4 | **Preseason pick-path changes of 2026-11-12/13** (season-end lookup `29e10bf`, cron season `1137cbe`, thin-slate checks `9998bbf`, `bts day-outcome` `222d18e` and its one cron line, 08:30 for yesterday, ruling R17). | B8a | **Restored-box execution suspended pending R.** Complete R before first normal boot or live activation of snapshot `446156433`. A live-mode deploy refuses when today's contest observation is unusable. **The season-boundary build of 2026-11-15 to 11-17 replaces B8's manual check** (change sets 1 to 4b-2, 6a, 5a, 4c, 6b-1 and 6b-2 on `main` as of 2026-11-18; 5b was NOT built and a malformed `decision.json` is an open hazard, both Eric's to decide; the whole-range review before the deploy is still to come; none of it may be deployed before that). In this order, BEFORE the deploy and before the scheduler is started on the restored box:
  • In `~/.bts-orchestrator.toml` set `contest_state_required = true` under `[scheduler]` AND `contest_state_expected = true` under `[health_checks]`, with `pick_delivery = "dm"` and `entry_intent = "enter"` (A5). With DM delivery and neither setting, `bts schedule` exits 2 before its first heartbeat and says why on stderr only: the deploy canary refuses the live configuration.
  • Run the target revision's `bts entry-intent --config ~/.bts-orchestrator.toml`: it must print `enter` and exit 0. Then `bash scripts/cron-setup-hetzner.sh show` and `install`.
  • The snapshot is from October: stop the scheduler, run `bts season-contract revoke --season 2027 --reason "restored from the offseason snapshot"` (it sets aside any manual observation and last season's saver flag), then `bts season-contract status`.
  • Each day until the post-enable `bts fetch-contest-streak` succeeds and `bts season-contract status` reports `automatic path alone: accepted` for the active ET season: `bts set-contest-streak --date --streak N --best-streak B --saver S` with N, B and S read from MLB. While the automatic path is refused, a day without a usable dated observation has no pick. The refusal names this command. **Enter it in the morning, before the scheduler's first lineup check.** The scheduler reads the state when it starts the day (10:00 ET, or an hour before an early first game) and DMs `Morning check for : no usable contest state was found at startup …` with the time of the first lineup check (change set 6b-1; no morning DM when that check is under ten minutes away, as on a 06:10 opener). An observation entered or corrected AFTER the day's pick was chosen does not re-pick by itself: the earlier pick is refused at delivery (change set 5a) and a new one is chosen only if a later lineup check or the fallback refresh still runs and its prediction succeeds. If none remains, that day has no pick. **Do not restart the scheduler to force a re-pick**: a restart can run two prediction passes and miss the cutoff, sleeps to the regular check on a thin slate, and mid-send leaves the day locked as unconfirmed (`build/cs5b-check/contract-check.md`).
  • Let `bts fetch-contest-streak` run (it records readings in the ledger only). When `bts season-contract status` shows readings that match MLB for some days: stop the scheduler, wait for any fetch, `bts season-contract enable --season 2027`, run `bts fetch-contest-streak`, then check that `bts season-contract status` reports `automatic path alone: accepted` for the active ET season. If the fetch fails or automatic status is refused, follow the diagnostics, keep filing daily dated observations and restart live scheduling with today's accepted dated observation while cutover is pending. If interrupted, verify fetch completion and current status before stopping daily observations. After the first successful, accepted automatic fetch, read `bts saver-state` for the active ET year. Initialize only if it reports `uninitialized`, using the actual MLB saver state with `bts saver-state --init --season `. Recheck the ET day and year before acting on earlier output. If a concurrent fetch initializes the flag first, reread it. Restart the scheduler.
  • **Expected false alarms in the first days (ruling R39; do not chase them):** `park_drag_freshness` pages `CRITICAL` at the end of Opening Night and until the first 07:45 refresh that sees a game (the table's last game is last September); and if the season is switched to automatic within its first two days, the contest-state health check can page `CRITICAL` for a missing `source_date` until MLB's ledger shows the first settled pick. Anything else, or either of these lasting past the third day, is real. A third expected alarm, only if Opening Night's pick locks while one team's lineup is still unposted (a thin early lock, ruling R18): the live-forward research capture for that date fails its row count (nine rows where ten are expected), `analytics_artifacts_missing` pages `CRITICAL`, and the resolution alert for that date warns from day 4 and is `CRITICAL` from day 7 without ageing out (ruling R41). It costs that one date's research capture and no pick; to quiet it, ask Claude to archive that date's capture directory by hand.
  • After the switch: a pick delivered on an automatic reading whose last accepted fetch is more than 14 hours old still goes out, with one `STALE CONTEST READING` warning DM that day (at the morning check if it is already stale then, otherwise after the pick is delivered; change set 4c) and a record on the pick file (`automatic_reading`). On that DM: check MLB; if the streak or saver differs, enter the day's dated observation (before the first check if it is the morning DM); then find out why the fetch stopped (`bts fetch-contest-streak`, its own failure DMs, cookies).
Do not run `bts schedule --dry-run` on the box as a probe: it writes the heartbeat and can idle. | Eric runs the box commands; Claude prepares them | `bts entry-intent` exit 0; `status` output before `enable`; post-enable fetch exit 0, `automatic path alone: accepted` for the active ET season, and the active-year saver read; the first day's morning DM (or the journal line `Morning state check: dated contest state accepted`) and the pick after the dated observation |

| B8b | **From the whole-range review (2026-11-19), until the open items land:** (1) during the days the season runs on dated observations, do NOT act on a contest-state alert that arrives between midnight ET and the morning wake after a late game: it is judged at the wall clock, after yesterday's observation expired, and its command template is dated before MLB has settled the night's pick; read `bts season-contract status` in the morning instead. (2) **Preserve the files in place during triage and make changes only as part of verified recovery directed by the BTS lead or Eric.** On a replay warning (`bts reconcile` prints `Season replay unavailable for <date> (<reason>); streak retained, not recalculated.`) or failed reconcile, preserve the files and paste the exact warning or error, ET run time, host, and receipt path if available into the supervised BTS lead Claude session (`bts-lead`), or send them to Eric for handoff if the session is unavailable. If yesterday's correction is at risk and the cutoff is still ahead, contact the lead or Eric immediately for assessment before 08:00 ET. After the cutoff, record any missed correction, and in either case get a decision before the next affected selection, grade, or entry check. If the pick file is unreadable or disagrees with the commitment, verify the pick, game and entry against MLB and the original delivery or private lock, and have the lead coordinate recovery before relying on automated entry checks, grading, or the dashboard. When this warning appears, the replay leaves `streak.json` unrecalculated and later grading can advance an incorrect model count or saver. On other failures, verify whether replay saved before deciding what needs recovery. Required live delivery uses a valid contest observation and refuses to pick without one. Model-only recommendations, previews, and shadow picks can already be affected, so investigate before the next model-dependent use and confirm a successful full replay after addressing the blockers. Never set a file aside on the strength of an empty MLB entry or a missing, false, or unreadable decision alone, because a private lock can precede its decision and successful delivery can precede its durable acknowledgement or post marker (`docs/reviews/2026-11-18-whole-range/STOP-C3.md`, `STOP-C3V.md`, `review-c3v-operator-text/`). (3) W12/W13 operate on this box only after D is shipped and verified with the guard and approved cron. installer provisions the scheduler's system-wide user-unit drop-in and the hold
